chujian.description: Chu Bamboo Slips, regional Warring States period writing from the state of Chu, around 300 BCE

jinwen.description: Bronze Script, ancient characters engraved or cast on ritual bronze vessels during the Shang and Zhou Dynasties, around 1046 BCE

chuanchao.description: Historical manual copying and manuscript transcription methods used to preserve ancient text characters across generations, popular in catalog compilations around 986 CE

calligraphyxing.description: Running Script (Xingshu), a fluid semi-cursive calligraphic style balancing speed and legibility, popularized around 353 CE

calligraphyli.description: Clerical Script (Lishu), a squared-off and highly efficient administrative script developed and widespread during the Han Dynasty, around 202 BCE

calligraphykai.description: Regular Script (Kaishu), the highly structured standard block-style handwriting born in the late Han and perfected during the Tang Dynasty, around 600 CE

calligraphycao.description: Cursive Script (Caoshu), a highly simplified and continuous artistic flowing script developed from the Han through Jin Dynasties, matured around 300 CE

jiaguwen.description: Oracle Bone Script, the oldest confirmed system of Chinese writing carved on animal bones and turtle shells during the late Shang Dynasty, around 1250 BCE

qinjian.description: Qin Bamboo Slips, administrative and legal records written on bamboo strips during the state of Qin and the Qin Dynasty, around 221 BCE

kaichengshijing.description: Kaicheng Stone Classics, twelve Confucian classics carved on 114 monumental stone tablets during the Tang Dynasty, completed in 837 CE

calligraphyzhuan.description: Seal Script (Zhuanshu), formal and stylized ancient script originating in the Zhou and standardized under the Qin Dynasty, around 221 BCE

hanjian.description: Han Bamboo Slips, wood and bamboo records providing immense insight into daily life and military border operations during the Han Dynasty, around 202 BCE

zengyun.description: Later phonetic rhyme extensions and manual updates used for classical poetry composition and civil service exams, compiled around 1300 CE

hongwuzhengyun.description: An official imperial rhyming standard dictionary commissioned by the Ming Dynasty's Hongwu Emperor, published in 1375 CE

standardj.description: Modern standard typographic glyph forms used for Japanese Kanji, tracking standards established from 1946 CE

guangyun.description: A massive and highly influential rime dictionary compiling Middle Chinese phonology during the Song Dynasty, published in 1008 CE

kangxi.description: The Kangxi Dictionary, a definitive imperial dictionary standardizing over 47,000 characters during the Qing Dynasty, published in 1716 CE

standardg.description: Modern standard typographic glyph forms used in Mainland China, formalized starting in 1980 CE

standardk.description: Modern standard typographic glyph forms used for Korean Hanja, cataloged under the KS X 1001 standard since 1987 CE

xipingshijing.description: Xiping Stone Classics, the earliest official stone-carved version of the Confucian classics established during the Eastern Han Dynasty, around 175 CE

houmamengshu.description: Houma Covenant Texts, brush-written alliance texts on jade and stone plaques from the late Spring and Autumn period, around 497 BCE

santishijing.description: Three-Style Stone Classics, Confucian texts carved in three parallel historical scripts during the Cao Wei period of the Three Kingdoms, around 240 CE
